---
title: Edit and find books in a Swift app
sidebar_label: Edit and find in a Swift app
description: Add editing to the Shelf app, see how the instance merges a change made offline, link books in their notes, and find books by title.
job: A builder adds editing, sees an offline merge, links books and finds them by title.
kind: tutorial
---

- **You'll build** a book page for Shelf, where you change a book, write notes that link to other books, and find books by title.
- **You need** the Shelf app from [Build an app with Swift](/build/swift-app), and your own Marfa instance with the CLI signed in, as the [Quickstart](/quickstart) leaves you.
- **You'll have** an app that edits offline, shows how the instance answered each change, and makes an [edge](/build/edges) for each link in a book's notes.

<Steps paged>
<Step>

### Open a book

Add an update to `Library`. It names the version of the book the change was based on:

```swift title="Library.swift"
    func update(_ book: Item, _ properties: JSONObject) async {
        await write { copy in
            try await copy.items.update(book.id, Edit(properties: properties, baseVersion: book.version))
        }
    }
```

**Send only the fields the person changed:** the instance merges an older change field by field, so a field sent unchanged can overwrite a newer value. Add a page for one book at the end of `ContentView.swift`:

```swift title="ContentView.swift"
struct BookView: View {
    let library: Library
    let book: Item
    @State private var title = ""
    @State private var progress = "planned"

    var body: some View {
        Form {
            TextField("Title", text: $title)
                .onSubmit { save(["title": .string(title)]) }
            Picker("Progress", selection: $progress) {
                ForEach(["planned", "started", "finished", "abandoned"], id: \.self) { Text($0.capitalized) }
            }
            .onChange(of: progress) { if progress != book.properties["progress"]?.string { save(["progress": .string(progress)]) } }
        }
        .disabled(book.readOnly)
        .navigationTitle(book.title ?? "Untitled")
        .onAppear {
            title = book.title ?? ""
            progress = book.properties["progress"]?.string ?? "planned"
        }
    }

    private func save(_ properties: JSONObject) { Task { await library.update(book, properties) } }
}
```

`progress` is a status field, whose values the [Media](/catalog/media) type lists. **`readOnly` is the instance's advice** that a connector keeps the item, so the page offers no editing. The copy takes the write either way.

In `ContentView`, wrap each row in a link:

```swift title="ContentView.swift"
                    NavigationLink(value: book.id) {
                        LabeledContent(book.title ?? "Untitled", value: book.properties["author"]?.string ?? "")
                    }
```

Add the destination after `.navigationTitle("Shelf")`. It finds the book again each time, so the page always holds its current version:

```swift title="ContentView.swift"
            .navigationDestination(for: String.self) { id in
                if let book = library.books?.value.first(where: { $0.id == id }) {
                    BookView(library: library, book: book)
                }
            }
```

Run the app, open Bleak House and set **Progress** to Started. **Changes** shows Sent.

</Step>
<Step>

### See a merge

Change the same book in two places, and the instance combines the changes by the type's rules.

1. Stop the server with `marfa server stop`.
2. In Shelf, change the title to `Bleak House (Penguin Classics)` and press Return. **Changes** shows Waiting to send.
3. Quit Shelf, so it can't send the change, and start the server with `marfa server start`.
4. Change the title on the server. The book is at version 2: the create, then the progress.

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa items update <book-id> --version 2 --prop "title=Bleak House: A Novel"
```

```text
marfa: writing to http://localhost:8600
updated core.media.book 01a1f134-05b9-70a9-ae2b-43825493170b "Bleak House: A Novel" (version 3)
```

</Terminal>

Run Shelf again. It sends the rename, based on version 2, and **Changes** shows Merged title with a newer change. **The title is Bleak House (Penguin Classics):** a book's `title` keeps the last change to reach the instance. A book's `body` and `notes` keep both, so two edits to them end `conflicted`, with yours in a conflicted copy. [Versions](/build/versions#when-two-apps-write-the-same-item) explains the rules.

</Step>
<Step>

### Link books

A link names another item in double brackets, such as `[[Middlemarch]]`. Marfa reads links only from a type's body field, which for a book is `body`, and **saving the `body` makes a `references` edge** to the item, which is why Shelf asked for `edge.references:write`. Add a check that shows what each link names while the person types, inside `Library`:

```swift title="Library.swift"
    func links(in text: String, of book: Item) async -> [LinkCandidates] {
        let targets = linkParts(in: text).map(\.target)
        guard let copy, !targets.isEmpty else { return [] }
        return (try? await copy.items.linkCandidates(of: targets, in: book.id)) ?? []
    }
```

`linkCandidates(of:in:)` answers what each link could name, from the copy alone. Add the notes at the end of `ContentView.swift`, and put `NotesSection(library: library, book: book)` last inside `BookView`'s `Form`:

```swift title="ContentView.swift"
struct NotesSection: View {
    let library: Library
    let book: Item
    @State private var text = ""
    @State private var links: [LinkCandidates] = []
    var body: some View {
        Section("About the book") {
            TextField("Notes, with links such as [[Middlemarch]]", text: $text, axis: .vertical)
            ForEach(links, id: \.target) { LabeledContent($0.target, value: describe($0)) }
            Button("Save Notes") { Task { await library.update(book, ["body": .string(text)]) } }
        }
        .onAppear { text = book.body ?? "" }
        .task(id: "\(text)\(book.version)") { links = await library.links(in: text, of: book) }
    }
    private func describe(_ link: LinkCandidates) -> String {
        switch link.state {
        case .bound: "Linked"
        case .ambiguous: "\(link.candidates.count) books have this title"
        case .unresolved: link.candidates.isEmpty ? "No book has this title" : "Links when you save"
        }
    }
}
```

A link is `bound` only once the copy knows its edge. One matching book is `unresolved` until you save, because the instance decides.

Run the app, open Bleak House, and type `Read after [[Middlemarch]], and compare [[Persuasion]].` Middlemarch shows Links when you save, and Persuasion shows No book has this title. Choose **Save Notes**. Middlemarch shows Linked, and the edge is on the instance:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa edges list --type references --limit 1
```

```text
id                                    type        created                   link
01a1f134-c861-76e3-9ce7-3622fd2b9922  references  2026-11-19T00:29:36.640Z  01a1f134-05b9-70a9-ae2b-43825493170b -> 01a1f134-0e1a-74d3-bcb6-c4446c4e3aea
```

</Terminal>

Persuasion gets no edge.

</Step>
<Step>

### Find books by title

Add a filter to `Library`. Assigning `reading` makes the query read again:

```swift title="Library.swift"
    func find(_ text: String) {
        var filters = ListFilters(types: ["core.media.book"])
        if !text.isEmpty {
            let title = FilterCondition(field: .property("title"), operator: .contains, value: .text(text))
            filters.filter = try? FilterExpression(conditions: [title]).encoded()
        }
        books?.reading = .list(filters)
    }
```

In `ContentView`, keep the search with `@AppStorage("search") private var search = ""` beside `session`. Add a search field after the destination:

```swift title="ContentView.swift"
            .searchable(text: $search, prompt: "Find by title")
            .onChange(of: search) { library.find(search) }
```

Then apply the saved search once the copy opens, by replacing the view's `.task`:

```swift title="ContentView.swift"
        .task {
            await library.open(signingInWith: session)
            library.find(search)
        }
```

Run the app and search for `Bleak`. The list shows Bleak House (Penguin Classics), read from the copy with no request. Quit and run again: the search stays. [List, filter and search](/build/list-filter-search) lists the other conditions.
